summary.name: HeyMate
summary.one_liner: HeyMate is a free, open-source macOS menu-bar-notch assistant that explains desktop apps and websites out loud, points at the next click, and runs approval-gated background agents on your own Claude, ChatGPT (Codex), or OpenCode subscription.
use_cases: learn a desktop app step by step
get unstuck in a website or app
ask questions about what is on screen
run approved background agents for routine tasks
summary.what_it_does: HeyMate sits in the MacBook notch. When you hold Control+Option and ask, it captures the screen, explains how to do something in the app or website in front of you, and points at the next click while waiting for you to act. It re-checks the screen after each step. Longer jobs go to named background agents that run on Claude Code, Codex, or OpenCode, plan first, and wait for approval before changing anything. It also offers calendar, reminders, notes and mail integrations, optional web integrations via Composio, and a privacy model that keeps data on the Mac except questions and screen context sent to the chosen AI.
notable: Points at the next click and waits while you try each step
Bring your own subscription: Claude, ChatGPT via Codex, OpenCode, or API keys, with no HeyMate fee
Background agents plan first and need approval; undo snapshots of local files
Screen is captured only when asked and between walkthrough steps; password managers and System Settings skipped by default
caveats: Requires macOS 14.2 or later; Apple Intelligence option needs macOS 26 and is text only
Screen guidance needs a vision-capable model
Provider usage limits and optional service charges still apply
Builds are self-signed and not notarized by Apple, so the DMG needs Open Anyway on first launch
